title: Encore - Psychology takes toys seriously, with Barry Kudrowitz, PhD, and Doris Bergen, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a winter break, so we're rerunning some of our favorite episodes from the paSt. In December 2021, I talked to psychologist Doris Bergen
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》正在进行冬歇，因此我们正在重播过去一些最受欢迎的单集。在2021年12月，我采访了心理学家多丽丝·博根

sentences.en: and toy designer Barry Kudrowitz about what makes a great toy, what makes some toys stand the test of time, and the importance of play for both children and adults.
sentences.zh: 以及玩具设计师巴里·库德罗维茨，探讨了是什么让一个玩具成为好玩具，为什么有些玩具能经受住时间的考验，以及游戏对儿童和成人的重要性。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back with new episodes in January.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》将于1月带着新节目回归。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: It's that time of year when parents and other caregivers race to find the hottest toys and stock up on classic favorites, from Poppets to Pokemon, from Squishmallows to Legos.
sentences.zh: 又到了每年的这个时候，父母和其他照顾者竞相寻找最热门的玩具，并囤积经典的挚爱，从泡泡按按乐到宝可梦，从棉花糖抱抱公仔到乐高。

sentences.en: Toys might seem frivolous, but to psychologists, they're a subject for serious study.
sentences.zh: 玩具看起来可能微不足道，但对心理学家来说，它们是一个需要严肃研究的课题。

sentences.en: Researchers have long known that children learn best through play.
sentences.zh: 研究人员早就知道，儿童通过游戏学得最好。

sentences.en: Play is how kids stretch their brains and develop crucial cognitive, social, and other skills.
sentences.zh: 游戏是孩子们舒展大脑、培养关键认知、社交以及其他技能的方式。

sentences.en: And toys are a fundamental part of playtime.
sentences.zh: 而玩具是游戏时间中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: But what makes something a good toy?
sentences.zh: 但什么才算是一个好玩具呢？

sentences.en: Indeed, what makes something a toy at all?
sentences.zh: 事实上，到底是什么让某种东西成为玩具？

sentences.en: Why do some toys stand the test of time, while others are just a one-season wonder?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些玩具经得起时间的考验，而另一些只是昙花一现？

sentences.en: What's the difference between fun and educational toys?
sentences.zh: 好玩和益智的玩具之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Why do we assign gender appropriateness to some toys and not to others?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们给某些玩具贴上性别合适的标签，而对其他玩具则不然？

sentences.en: How do kids' toy preferences change as they age?
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，孩子们对玩具的偏好是如何改变的？

sentences.en: And how has technology changed what toys are and the way kids play with toys?
sentences.zh: 科技又是如何改变玩具的本质以及孩子们玩玩具的方式的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: Our first is Dr. Barry Kudrowitz, an associate professor and director of product design at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, where he teaches classes in toy product design.
sentences.zh: 第一位是巴里·库德罗维茨博士，他是明尼苏达大学双城分校产品设计的副教授兼主任，他在那里教授玩具产品设计课程。

sentences.en: Dr. Kudrowitz has a PhD in mechanical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士拥有麻省理工学院机械工程博士学位，

sentences.en: Technology, where he studied creativity, humor, and idea generation.
sentences.zh: 他在那里研究创造力、幽默感和创意生成。

sentences.en: And he has studied how play can fuel creativity and innovation.
sentences.zh: 他还研究了游戏如何能激发创造力和创新。

sentences.en: In addition to his academic career, he's also a toy designer.
sentences.zh: 除了学术生涯，他也是一名玩具设计师。

sentences.en: Highlights of his work include the Ketchup Crapper, an anthropomorphic roller skating ketchup bottle
sentences.zh: 他的代表作包括番茄酱大便器，一个拟人化的滑轮番茄酱瓶，

sentences.en: that he designed as a grad student, and the Nerf Atom Blaster, a Nerf toy sold by Hasbro more than five years.
sentences.zh: 这是他在读研究生时设计的，还有Nerf原子发射器，一款由孩之宝销售了五年多的Nerf玩具。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Dr. Doris Bergen, a distinguished professor emerita of educational psychology at Miami University in Oxford, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是多丽丝·博根博士，她是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学教育心理学的杰出荣休教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Bergen began her career as a pre-kindergarten and elementary school teacher.
sentences.zh: 博根博士的职业生涯始于学前班和小学老师。

sentences.en: And over her long academic career, she has explored the many ways that play is crucial to children's development.
sentences.zh: 在她漫长的学术生涯中，她探讨了游戏对儿童发展至关重要的多种方式。

sentences.en: She has studied play and humor in early and middle childhood, the effects of technology-enhanced toys, and cross-cultural considerations in play, among many other topics.
sentences.zh: 她研究了儿童早期和中期的游戏与幽默、科技增强型玩具的影响以及游戏中的跨文化考量等众多主题。

sentences.en: Dr. Bergen has authored or edited more than a dozen books, including her most recent, The Handbook of Developmentally Appropriate Toys, which was published in March 2021.
sentences.zh: 博根博士撰写或编辑了十多本书，其中包括她最近于2021年3月出版的《发展适宜性玩具手册》。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: All right, so let's start with a broad question, which we usually do.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们先从一个宏观的问题开始，我们通常都这样做。

sentences.en: What is the purpose of toys and what makes something a good toy or makes something a toy at all?
sentences.zh: 玩具的目的是什么，是什么让一个玩具成为好玩具，或者说是什么让某种东西成为玩具？

sentences.en: For example, can a stick or a rock be a toy?
sentences.zh: 例如，一根树枝或一块石头可以成为玩具吗？

sentences.en: Actually, toys have existed for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，玩具已经存在了很长、很长的时间。

sentences.en: You can even find them in early sights.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在早期的遗址中找到它们。

sentences.en: And so some of the typical toys that children still play with today, like dolls and wheel toys, things of that sort, have been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 因此，孩子们今天仍在玩的某些典型玩具，比如洋娃娃和轮式玩具之类的事情，已经存在了很长时间。

sentences.en: But I would say that the purpose of toys, in my view, is to enhance children's play because children will play even if there aren't any toys.
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，在我看来，玩具的目的是为了增强儿童的游戏，因为即使没有任何玩具，孩子们也会玩。

sentences.en: They'll find sticks or they'll find rocks or they'll find other things to use in their pretend play and in their gameplay.
sentences.zh: 他们会在假装游戏和游戏玩法中寻找树枝、石头或其他东西来使用。

sentences.en: But toys are a means of enhancing the play and making it more creative and often more elaborate.
sentences.zh: 但玩具是增强游戏、使其更具创造力且通常更精致的一种手段。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: Toys are a tool for for play.
sentences.zh: 玩具是游戏的工具。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a difference between a toy and a toy product.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，玩具和玩具产品之间是有区别的。

sentences.en: There are certain toys that are designed by people to be intended to be used for play.
sentences.zh: 有些玩具是人们设计出来专门用于游戏的。

sentences.en: And then there's things that are not designed, you know, intended to be used for play that children still play with, like cardboard boxes and spoons and rakes and stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些并非设计用于游戏，但孩子们仍然在玩的物品，比如纸盒、勺子、耙子之类的，对吧？

sentences.en: There's still toys, but maybe they're not toy products.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然是玩具，但也许它们不是玩具产品。

sentences.en: And many toy products are designed by people who have ideas about what they think is good for children to play with.
sentences.zh: 许多玩具产品是由那些对儿童玩什么好有想法的人设计的。

sentences.en: Maybe they think they'll learn particular things from them.
sentences.zh: 也许他们认为孩子们会从中学习到特定的东西。

sentences.en: They have different expectations about the toys.
sentences.zh: 他们对玩具有着不同的期望。

sentences.en: And I would say a really good toy is one that doesn't do everything itself, but has the child do it.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，一个真正的好玩具不是自己包办一切，而是让孩子自己去玩。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, I think some toys designed do too much and there isn't really even room for children to do very much with them.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我认为有些设计的玩具做得太多了，甚至没有留给孩子们太多自己动手的空间。

sentences.en: And so those toys typically don't have very lasting value.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些玩具通常没有太持久的价值。

sentences.en: Maybe kids will play with them for a while, learn what they do, and then they'll probably turn them into something else and use them in a different way or maybe discard
sentences.zh: 也许孩子们会玩一会儿，了解它们的功能，然后可能会把它们变成别的东西，以不同的方式使用它们，或者干脆丢弃

sentences.en: them altogether.
sentences.zh: 它们。

sentences.en: And are those things that you think about, Dr. Kudrowitz, when you're designing toys or teaching people how to design toys?
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，当你在设计玩具或教人们如何设计玩具时，你会考虑这些事情吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm thinking about them, but not necessarily the students.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在考虑，但学生们不一定。

sentences.en: And even when we do playtesting, it's not necessarily even the children that we playtest are thinking about those things.
sentences.zh: 即使我们进行游戏测试，我们测试游戏的儿童也不一定在考虑这些事情。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, it's what is trendy or popular that they might gravitate to.
sentences.zh: 通常，他们可能会被时髦或受欢迎的东西所吸引。

sentences.en: But I also think that what makes a toy a good toy is that it can be used in a variety of different contexts and it doesn't die.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，让一个玩具成为好玩具的原因是它可以在各种不同的上下文中使用，而且它不会过时。

sentences.en: You know, you can use it for generations, for example, or in multiple different ways of playing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，例如你可以用它好几代，或者用多种不同的方式来玩。

sentences.en: You know, like the cardboard box is a great example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像纸板箱就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: We actually have a box in our dining room right now from a couch, but it's been played with by the children for months now.
sentences.zh: 我们餐厅里现在实际上就有一个沙发的包装箱，但孩子们已经玩了好几个月了。

sentences.en: And we left it this giant box in the in the dining room.
sentences.zh: 我们把这个巨大的箱子留在了餐厅里。

sentences.en: And they play with that more than, you know, all the toys we've gotten so far.
sentences.zh: 他们玩这个箱子的时间，比我们迄今为止买的所有玩具加起来还要多。

sentences.en: It's a fort.
sentences.zh: 它是一个堡垒。

sentences.en: It's a rocket ship.
sentences.zh: 它是一艘火箭飞船。

sentences.en: They're drawing all over the walls.
sentences.zh: 他们在墙上到处画画。

sentences.en: They're cutting out holes.
sentences.zh: 他们在上面戳洞。

sentences.en: And that was free.
sentences.zh: 而且那是免费的。

sentences.en: And it's compostable.
sentences.zh: 而且它是可堆肥的。

sentences.en: And I think it's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太棒了。

sentences.en: There are sort of different kinds of play, you know, of course, and different kinds of toys facilitate different kinds.
sentences.zh: 当然，游戏有不同的种类，不同的玩具促进不同的种类。

sentences.en: If you're thinking of just kind of exploratory play or manipulative play, that's one kind of toy that will work for that.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑的只是探索性游戏或操作性游戏，那是适用于此的一种玩具。

sentences.en: If you're looking at pretend play, there's a whole range of other kinds of toys that are really facilitative of pretense.
sentences.zh: 如果你在寻找假装游戏，还有整整一系列其他类型的玩具非常有助于假装。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's game play of all different kinds and very different kinds of toys for that.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有各种各样的游戏玩法，并且有非常不同类型的玩具适用于这些玩法。

sentences.en: And there's certainly some overlap among those.
sentences.zh: 这些之间肯定有一些重叠。

sentences.en: But the type of play that the child is going to do, if it's active play, quiet play, or of various sorts, will usually need, or at least there'll be an expectation
sentences.zh: 但是孩子将要玩的游戏类型，无论是活跃的游戏、安静的游戏，还是各种各样的游戏，通常都需要，或者至少会有这样的期望

sentences.en: that different kinds of toys will meet the needs for different kinds of play.
sentences.zh: 即不同种类的玩具将满足不同类型游戏的需求。

sentences.en: So a lot of parents think that toys come in basically two categories.
sentences.zh: 所以很多父母认为玩具基本上分为两大类。

sentences.en: And Dr. Bergen, you just described several categories, not just two, but for parents, they think they're educational toys,
sentences.zh: 博根博士，你刚才描述了好几个类别，不仅仅是两个，但对父母来说，他们认为有益智玩具，

sentences.en: like those that are designed to teach science or math or reading.
sentences.zh: 比如那些旨在教授科学、数学或阅读的玩具。

sentences.en: And then there are toys that are for fun, which covers pretty much everything else.
sentences.zh: 然后是供娱乐的玩具，这几乎涵盖了所有其他玩具。

sentences.en: Is that a valid distinction?
sentences.zh: 这种区分有效吗？

sentences.en: And is there a difference between a fun toy and an educational toy?
sentences.zh: 好玩的玩具和益智玩具有区别吗？

sentences.en: Should there be?
sentences.zh: 应该有区别吗？

sentences.en: I mean, going back to the very first thing we talked about, the primary purpose of a toy is play.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回到我们讨论的第一件事，玩具的主要目的是游戏。

sentences.en: And if the primary purpose is to teach something, it may not be a very good toy.
sentences.zh: 如果主要目的是教导某些东西，那它可能不是一个好玩具。

sentences.en: But that being said, play is how we learn.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，游戏就是我们学习的方式。

sentences.en: That's how we've learned skills growing up.
sentences.zh: 那是我们在成长过程中学习技能的方式。

sentences.en: We learned developmental skills, cognitive skills, physical skills.
sentences.zh: 我们学习发展技能、认知技能、身体技能。

sentences.en: And so you could also argue that no matter what kind of play, if you're engaging in play, you could argue that you're learning something.
sentences.zh: 所以你也可以争辩说，无论哪种游戏，只要你参与了游戏，你就可以说你学到了一些东西。

sentences.en: And so it's a little bit hard to separate those two.
sentences.zh: 所以要将这两者分开有点难。

sentences.en: But I don't necessarily like the idea of a toy being primarily designed to be teaching you something.
sentences.zh: 但我并不一定喜欢把玩具主要设计来教你某些东西的想法。

sentences.en: I would agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: I think that's maybe more of a marketing distinction than it is a toy distinction, because I think children learn from every type of play and from every type of toy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能更多是营销上的区分，而不是玩具本身的区分，因为我认为孩子们从每一种游戏和每一种玩具中都能学习。

sentences.en: They may not be learning a specific thing like letters or, you know, whatever the toy maker thought they would do.
sentences.zh: 他们可能没有学到像字母或玩具制造商认为他们会做的特定事情。

sentences.en: But they also learn many other social and physical and intellectual skills from just about any toy.
sentences.zh: 但他们也从几乎任何玩具中学到了许多其他社交、身体和智力技能。

sentences.en: So I think the distinction educational toys is primarily a distinction for parents and for teachers and
sentences.zh: 所以我认为益智玩具这个区分主要是针对父母、老师以及

sentences.en: people who think that, oh, if it says educational, it's going to have a greater educational factor.
sentences.zh: 那些认为“哦，如果它标明是益智的，它就会有更大的教育价值”的人。

sentences.en: The other way that educational toy could be seen is if there's a specific kind of teaching that the adult wants the child to have.
sentences.zh: 看待益智玩具的另一种方式是，如果成年人希望孩子获得某种特定的教学。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, sometimes those kind of toys that are very specifically designed to teach a certain thing are either not used very often by the child or the
sentences.zh: 而不幸的是，有时那些专门设计来教授某种特定事物的玩具，要么不经常被孩子使用，要么

sentences.en: child transforms them in some way into pretend or something else.
sentences.zh: 孩子以某种方式将它们转化为假装游戏或其他东西。

sentences.en: And they don't exactly use them in the same way that the person who designed them thought they would use them.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有完全按照设计它们的人想象的那样去使用它们。

sentences.en: And I think that's an amazing thing that kids can do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是孩子们能做的一件了不起的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, I've known parents, for example, who've decided that they never want their children to have a toy gun.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认识一些父母，例如，他们决定永远不让他们的孩子拥有玩具枪。

sentences.en: And somehow kids will figure out how to make something into a gun.
sentences.zh: 而不知何故，孩子们会想方设法把某种东西做成枪。

sentences.en: If they want to play with guns, they're going to have a make-believe gun, right?
sentences.zh: 如果他们想玩打仗游戏，他们就会有一把假想的枪，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just the creative end of childhood.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是童年的创造力所在。

sentences.en: Dr. Kudrowitz, you were quoted in a recent article talking about the fact that toy makers worry that kids are losing interest in toys at a younger age than they used to.
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，最近的一篇文章引用了你的话，谈到了玩具制造商担心孩子们对玩具失去兴趣的年龄比过去更早这一事实。

sentences.en: Is that actually happening?
sentences.zh: 这真的在发生吗？

sentences.en: And if it is, why do you think so?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你认为为什么会这样？

sentences.en: So this is related to the concept of age compression.
sentences.zh: 这与年龄压缩的概念有关。

sentences.en: There's probably other terms related to this.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他与此相关的术语。

sentences.en: We've talked to Doris about that.
sentences.zh: 我们已经和多丽丝讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: But it seems like kids are playing with the stuff that the older kids were playing with in the paSt. And this may be more of
sentences.zh: 但看起来现在的孩子在玩大孩子过去玩的东西。这可能更多是

sentences.en: an artifact of technology advancing to the degree that things that we used to play with in the past
sentences.zh: 科技发展到一定程度的一个产物，过去我们玩的东西

sentences.en: were, I don't want to say dumb, but they didn't have a high tech inside because that was expensive.
sentences.zh: 我不想说它们很笨，但它们的内部没有高科技，因为那很昂贵。

sentences.en: And in today's society, you can put LEDs in anything and it's relatively low coSt. You could put motors
sentences.zh: 在当今社会，你可以在任何东西里面装上LED灯，而且成本相对较低。你可以在

sentences.en: in things and processors and there's computers and everything, you know, in my pocket right now.
sentences.zh: 东西里装上马达和处理器，而且到处都有电脑，你知道的，现在就在我的口袋里。

sentences.en: And it's not that much more expensive in today's society.
sentences.zh: 在当今社会，它没有那么昂贵。

sentences.en: And so a lot of the things that children are playing with today are not necessarily video games, but they're more like technology.
sentences.zh: 因此，孩子们今天玩的很多东西不一定是电子游戏，但它们更像是科技产品。

sentences.en: And in the market space, some of those things kind of get lumped into consumer electronics and not necessarily in the toy aisle.
sentences.zh: 在市场领域，其中一些东西被归入消费电子产品，而不一定在玩具货架上。

sentences.en: And so again, it kind of goes back to maybe marketing in some ways, but also you're not necessarily seeing kids play with the same toys as they were years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，它在某种程度上又回到了营销问题，但你也确实不一定看到孩子们在玩几年前的那些同款玩具了。

sentences.en: And there's a lot more screens and digital things in their hands.
sentences.zh: 而且他们手里有更多的屏幕和数字设备。

sentences.en: As a long time observer of play and interviewing of adults' memories of their childhood play,
sentences.zh: 作为一名长期的游戏观察者以及对成年人童年游戏记忆的采访者，

sentences.en: I definitely agree with Barry that the way play, the time and the experiences children have in play now has changed quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我绝对同意巴里的看法，即现在游戏的方式、时间和儿童在游戏中的体验已经发生了相当大的变化。

sentences.en: When you think back to your own play time, or certainly many other people who I've interviewed, they recall long periods of time where they pretty much could decide what they
sentences.zh: 当你回想你自己的游戏时间，或者肯定还有我采访过的许多其他人，他们回想起很长一段时间里，他们几乎可以决定

sentences.en: wanted to do with the time.
sentences.zh: 他们想用这些时间做什么。

sentences.en: And the kind of play materials they had were ones that they created, they made the toy talk, or they made the toy walk, or they did whatever it was with their own imagination.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有的游戏材料是他们自己创造的，他们让玩具说话，让玩具走路，或者用他们自己的想象力做任何事情。

sentences.en: And now, so many of the toys, the toy does everything, there's really not much for the child to do.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这么多的玩具，玩具包办了一切，真的没有留给孩子多少事情可做了。

sentences.en: And so that toy is not going to be nearly as important in terms of children's development, or their interest level.
sentences.zh: 因此，就儿童的发展或他们的兴趣水平而言，这个玩具不会那么重要。

sentences.en: Because if you're just, there's 10 buttons to push, and you've pushed all 10 buttons, and then that's really the end of what you can do with the toy.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你只是，有10个按钮可以按，而你已经按完了所有的10个按钮，那么这真的是你对这个玩具能做的全部了。

sentences.en: Usually what you see the child do is either put it away and not look at it anymore, or pick it up and pretend it's something
sentences.zh: 通常你会看到孩子做的是要么把它收起来再也不看了，要么把它拿起来假装它是完全不同的东西

sentences.en: altogether different and use imagination and do something else with it.
sentences.zh: 并发挥想象力用它做别的事情。

sentences.en: So I do think that that change, and certainly that idea that experiences have gone down to lower levels is not just related
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为这种变化，当然还有体验下降到更低水平的想法，不仅与

sentences.en: to toys, but it's pervasive across a lot of other things for children today.
sentences.zh: 玩具有关，而且在当今儿童的许多其他事情中也是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: But I do think, I've often thought the people designing the technology are the ones that are having the playful time.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，我经常觉得设计科技产品的人才是真正享受游戏时光的人。

sentences.en: Because they're the ones that get to figure out what to do with it, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是能够弄清楚如何使用它等等的人。

sentences.en: So it's the grown-ups who are coming up with these ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以是成年人在想出这些主意。

sentences.en: The kids aren't asking for the toys to be, yeah.
sentences.zh: 孩子们并没有要求玩具变成那样，是的。

sentences.en: So are you recommending that parents give their kids dolls that don't do anything except sit there?
sentences.zh: 所以你是在建议父母给孩子买那些除了坐在那里什么都不做的洋娃娃吗？

sentences.en: They still make those.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在制造那些。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: One of the things that concerns me a great deal is, if you remember back to your childhood, maybe all summer you didn't have anything to do
sentences.zh: 让我非常担心的一件事是，如果你回想起你的童年，也许整个夏天你都没有什么事可做，

sentences.en: except just figure out what to play with yourself.
sentences.zh: 除了自己琢磨玩什么。

sentences.en: Now children's lives are very structured, both after school and in summer, and so they don't necessarily have those long periods of time
sentences.zh: 现在孩子的生活安排得非常紧凑，无论是放学后还是夏天，所以他们不一定有那些大段的时间

sentences.en: where they can really create their own play world.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在其中真正创造自己的游戏世界。

sentences.en: So that's a very, very different thing that we see now.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们现在看到的非常非常不同的现象。

sentences.en: So let me ask a kind of a developmental question.
sentences.zh: 那我来问一个关于发展心理学的问题。

sentences.en: Maybe this is for Dr. Bergen, although you're both welcome to answer it, but what happens to children who grow up without actual toys?
sentences.zh: 也许这个问题是问博根博士的，虽然你们两位都可以回答，但是在实际玩具中长大的孩子会怎么样？

sentences.en: Do they develop differently, and are they different as adults?
sentences.zh: 他们的发展会有所不同吗？成年后他们会有所不同吗？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: I really don't know of any research that's really looked at children who grow up without play, because the
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道有任何研究真正关注过在没有游戏的环境中长大的孩子，因为

sentences.en: research that, let's say, would be done in a country where there were very few toys show that children play anyway.
sentences.zh: 比方说，在一个几乎没有什么玩具的国家所做的研究表明，孩子们无论如何都会玩。

sentences.en: They don't necessarily have to have toys to play.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定非得有玩具才能玩。

sentences.en: So it's more of a question, I guess, if you had children who had to go to work at age six or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以这更像是一个假设问题，如果你有六岁就得去上班之类的孩子。

sentences.en: And I don't really know.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太清楚。

sentences.en: That's a very important issue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: It probably should be studied, but I don't really know of the case that there are children who haven't any play experiences.
sentences.zh: 这或许应该被研究，但我真的不知道有哪个孩子没有任何游戏经历的案例。

sentences.en: But they may be very different kinds of play experiences.
sentences.zh: 但他们可能会有非常不同种类的游戏经历。

sentences.en: They may have play experiences where they use whatever is in their environment and create their own play as compared to the kind of play that Barry was mentioning, where they have
sentences.zh: 他们可能会利用环境中的任何东西来创造自己的游戏，与巴里刚才提到那种相比

sentences.en: many, many toys, but a lot of toys have all these characteristics that just require you to push a button or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多很多的玩具，但很多玩具都有各种各样的特点，只需要你按一下按钮之类的。

sentences.en: So I think there's a wide range of play experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为游戏经历的范围很广。

sentences.en: But at least in my experience, children, even if they have 10 or 15 minutes of their own time are going to find something to play.
sentences.zh: 但至少根据我的经验，孩子们哪怕只有10到15分钟自己的时间，也会找点东西来玩。

sentences.en: Going back to the last thing that Dora said, on technology, maybe restricting play.
sentences.zh: 回到多拉刚才关于科技可能会限制游戏的最后一点。

sentences.en: And that is true.
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此。

sentences.en: That happens.
sentences.zh: 这种情况确实会发生。

sentences.en: But it can also be used for good.
sentences.zh: 但它也可以被用于好的方面。

sentences.en: And designers can create open-ended play experiences for children, taking advantage of technology.
sentences.zh: 设计师可以利用科技为孩子们创造开放式的游戏体验。

sentences.en: So they could create new types of musical instruments or things where children can program their own things to do whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们可以创造出新型的乐器，或者让孩子们可以自己编程去做他们想做的事情的东西。

sentences.en: What is the Spider-Man quote?
sentences.zh: 蜘蛛侠的经典台词是什么来着？

sentences.en: With great power comes great responsibility.
sentences.zh: 能力越大，责任越大。

sentences.en: It's in the hands of the designer to create those good toys.
sentences.zh: 制造这些好玩具的重任就在设计师手中。

sentences.en: I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点。

sentences.en: I just think that if there's only one way to use a toy, that it's hard for children to use it for a long time period.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，如果一种玩具只有一种玩法，孩子们就很难长时间使用它。

sentences.en: So as long as there are many different things to do with it, even if it's got a lot of technology enhancement, I think it can be a toy that has a lot of playability.
sentences.zh: 所以，只要用它能做很多不同的事情，即使它有很多科技含量，我也认为它会是一个可玩性很高的玩具。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Kudrowitz, one for you.
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，这个问题留给你。

sentences.en: Do commercial toy designers think about developmental psychology while they're designing toys?
sentences.zh: 商业玩具设计师在设计玩具时会考虑发展心理学吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do toy companies routinely have psychologists that they consult with, that they have them on staff?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，玩具公司通常会有他们咨询的心理学家吗？或者他们有专职心理学家吗？

sentences.en: And are those toys different or better?
sentences.zh: 这些玩具会有所不同或更好吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think this is probably a question for Doris because I think she's consulted for those big companies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这可能得问多is，因为我觉得她为那些大公司做过咨询。

sentences.en: But I can say that not all toy companies are large and can afford consultation.
sentences.zh: 但我可以肯定地说，并非所有玩具公司都是大公司，都请得起咨询顾问。

sentences.en: And so it's probably generally the big players that could bring in consultants like Doris on these things.
sentences.zh: 所以通常只有大企业才会在这类事情上请像多is这样的顾问。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll pick up on that because I did and a lot of other developmental psychology people did do a lot of work for Fisher Price.
sentences.zh: 是的，我来接着说，因为我和许多其他发展心理学领域的人确实为费雪做过大量工作。

sentences.en: They had their headquarters in New York at one time for a long one time.
sentences.zh: 他们曾经在纽约设立过很长一段时间的总部。

sentences.en: And they would bring us there and we would look at the toys at the stage before they were in their final stage.
sentences.zh: 他们会把我们请到那里，让我们在玩具完成最终定型之前的阶段去观察它们。

sentences.en: And we would evaluate them and, you know, describe what we thought might be good developmental aspects and what would work and what wouldn't and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们会对它们进行评估，你知道的，描述我们认为哪些可能是好的发展方面，什么行得通，什么行不通，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And that was really a very important thing.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一件非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: And that's why Fisher Price toys were always so very playable and very good for development.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么费雪的玩具总是那么好玩，对儿童的发育也非常有益。

sentences.en: Once Fisher Price got taken over, I think, by another company, I don't think they still have those consultants that they did at that time.
sentences.zh: 我想费雪被另一家公司收购后，他们可能就不再拥有当年那样的咨询顾问了。

sentences.en: But there may be some other toy companies that do have consultants.
sentences.zh: 但可能还有其他玩具公司确实有咨询顾问。

sentences.en: But I always thought that was really a good process because it was at the time of where there could still be some fine tuning of the toy, but the basic toy was already designed.
sentences.zh: 但我一直认为这是一个非常好的流程，因为当时还可以对玩具进行一些微调，而基础玩具已经设计好了。

sentences.en: And I think that made the toys really more playable and more developmentally appropriate by having that input from a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，通过引入心理学家的意见，真的让玩具变得更好玩、更符合儿童发展阶段。

sentences.en: Dr. Bergen, you studied play in China.
sentences.zh: 博根博士，你研究过中国的游戏。

sentences.en: Dr. Kudrowitz, you worked on toy design in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，你在荷兰从事过玩具设计。

sentences.en: Do the types of toys that kids like to play with vary much around the world, or are they pretty much universal?
sentences.zh: 孩子们喜欢玩的玩具类型在世界各地差异很大，还是基本上是通用的？

sentences.en: Dr. I guess I would say, as far as China, I didn't see any big differences.
sentences.zh: 博士，我想我会说，就中国而言，我没看到什么大的差异。

sentences.en: When I was there, there wasn't a lot of, where I was, it was not a rich environment, and so a lot of the play was pretty basic.
sentences.zh: 我在那里的时候，环境并不富裕，我呆的地方不是一个富裕的环境，所以很多游戏都非常基础。

sentences.en: But, you know, things like balls and dolls and toy trucks and various things like that were pretty much the same there.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，像球、洋娃娃、玩具卡车以及诸如此类的各种东西，在那里基本上都是一样的。

sentences.en: They also played a lot of games outdoors, and outdoor play was very big at the time I was in China.
sentences.zh: 他们还玩很多户外游戏，在我呆在中国的时候，户外游戏非常盛行。

sentences.en: I really don't know what it's like now, but that was quite a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道现在是什么样子，但那是相当久以前的事了。

sentences.en: What about in the Netherlands?
sentences.zh: 荷兰的情况呢？

sentences.en: It wasn't too different.
sentences.zh: 也没有太大区别。

sentences.en: I'm always looking for new stuff.
sentences.zh: 我总是在寻找新奇的东西。

sentences.en: And so being in a new environment, I felt inspired, and I felt like all the toys were cooler there, because they're all, you know, different.
sentences.zh: 因此身处新的环境中，我感到备受启发，我觉得那里的所有玩具都更酷，因为它们，你知道的，都很不一样。

sentences.en: But I was just on sabbatical, actually, a couple years ago there.
sentences.zh: 不过，其实我几年前刚去那里进行学术休假。

sentences.en: And it was my first introduction to Montessori.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次接触蒙台梭利教育。

sentences.en: And so we had our two-year-old in a Montessori daycare.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把两岁的孩子送进了一家蒙台梭利日托中心。

sentences.en: And that style of play was really exciting.
sentences.zh: 那种游戏风格真的让人很兴奋。

sentences.en: The toys are like real stuff.
sentences.zh: 那些玩具就像真的一样。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, prepping vegetables, you know, and cleaning and stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，准备蔬菜，你知道的，还有打扫卫生之类的事情。

sentences.en: And it's turning these everyday activities, you know, into play in some ways.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，它把这些日常活动转化成了游戏。

sentences.en: They have these kinder borderei, which are these kinder children farms, I guess, in the city.
sentences.zh: 他们有那种儿童农场，我想大概就是城里的儿童农场吧。

sentences.en: And you bring your, you know, family goes, and the kids take care of the animals, and they harvest vegetables.
sentences.zh: 你可以带，你知道的，全家人一起去，孩子们照顾动物，收割蔬菜。

sentences.en: And they can go and they take these little tiny kid-sized wheelbarrows and shovels, and they go into the pasture, and they pick up cow poop.
sentences.zh: 他们还可以去拿这些小巧的儿童尺寸的独轮车和铲子，走到牧场里去收集牛粪。

sentences.en: And they do that for like an hour.
sentences.zh: 他们可以干这个大概一个小时。

sentences.en: And it's like, and it's play.
sentences.zh: 而且这就像是，这其实就是游戏。

sentences.en: This sounds like a con.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是个骗局。

sentences.en: This is how you make children do work.
sentences.zh: 这就是你让孩子干活的方式。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: And my son is like, can we go back to the farm and do more of that?
sentences.zh: 我儿子会说，我们能回农场再做点那个吗？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And it's, it's getting out into nature, connecting with animals.
sentences.zh: 而且这，这就是走到大自然中去，与动物亲密接触。

sentences.en: You know, these are tools that aren't usually their size.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些通常不是他们那个尺寸的工具。

sentences.en: And so there's some novelty about that, too.
sentences.zh: 所以这也带来了一些新奇感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that European play researchers have studied a lot of outdoor play, because they're
sentences.zh: 而且我认为欧洲的游戏研究人员对户外游戏进行了大量研究，因为他们

sentences.en: very much more focused on the natural environment and doing things outdoors in many of the countries in Europe.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲的许多国家，他们更加关注自然环境以及在户外开展活动。

sentences.en: Not so much here as they do there, but that's been a very strong emphasis, I think, in Europe altogether.
sentences.zh: 这里不像那里那样重视，但我认为这一直是欧洲整体上非常强烈的重点。

sentences.en: I think, though, that what I've found is that children's types of play are very similar wherever you are.
sentences.zh: 不过，我发现无论身处何地，孩子们的游戏类型都非常相似。

sentences.en: And it may be that they use a manufactured toy that is designed specifically for something.
sentences.zh: 情况可能是他们使用专门为某种目的设计的量产玩具。

sentences.en: Or if they're in an environment where there isn't a manufactured toy that fits whatever it is they want to do, they can invent something else to use.
sentences.zh: 或者如果他们身处的环境中没有符合他们任何心愿的量产玩具，他们也能发明出别的东西来用。

sentences.en: You can use a piece of wood to be a truck if you want to, if you don't have a real truck.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有真正的卡车，你完全可以用一块木头当卡车。

sentences.en: You can use a rag and a ball to be a baby if you really don't have a real doll.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的没有真正的洋娃娃，你可以用一块抹布和一个球当婴儿。

sentences.en: So I don't think that necessarily the types of things children play are that different.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为孩子们玩的玩具类型会有那么大的不同。

sentences.en: I do think that there are many different materials they use in different places.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为他们在不同地方使用的材料会有很多差异。

sentences.en: But pretend play and game play and exploratory practice play, just doing over and over and expanding things, those are all very common types of play that you would see just really
sentences.zh: 但是假装游戏、规则游戏和探索性练习游戏，不断重复并扩展事物，这些都是非常常见的游戏类型，你真的可以看到

sentences.en: wherever you were in the world, I think.
sentences.zh: 无论你身处世界的哪个角落，我想都是如此。

sentences.en: So I mentioned in the intro that Dr. Kudrowitz, one of your first toy designs was a pooping ketchup bottle.
sentences.zh: 我在引言中提到过，库德罗维茨博士，你的第一个玩具设计是一个会拉粑粑的番茄酱瓶。

sentences.en: And Dr. Bergen, you've been quoted in a couple of recent articles about why kids are so interested in potty humor and toys that defecate.
